title: A Spire for the Ember
premise: Yara Amberdale has spent her life in Emberhollow, a valley where magic cannot enter, believing her oath-bound gift of swordspeech died with her mother. When she finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy, she learns the valley is not a refuge but a cage built by the first swordspeakers to starve an ancient war of its fuel—and she is the ember meant to end it. Hunted by the ash-priests who wrote the prophecy and pursued by a deserter who claims to be her mother's oath-partner, Yara must decide whether to break the valley's ward and let magic back into the world. In the end, she speaks her own name into the blade instead of the war-god's, shattering the prophecy and binding the magic to choice rather than blood—at the cost of the valley's protection and the only home she has ever known.
about_author: Tamsin Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-books before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about inheritance and the lies families tell to survive, and lives somewhere with too much rain and not enough ghosts.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Supposed to Exist
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the eve of the valley's Founding Festival, Yara discovers her own birthdate and today's date inked in a sealed prophecy book hidden beneath her mother's forge. She dismisses it as forgery until the ink moves. Emotional beat: quiet unease curdling into the vertigo of realizing her invisible life was designed by someone else.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She tests the ward at the valley's edge and finds it thinning—her swordspeech, dormant all her life, whispers through a rusted blade. Elder Maren catches her and lies badly about the valley's founding. Emotional beat: first taste of power tangled with the first taste of institutional betrayal.

chapters.title: The Deserter at the Ford
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A scarred stranger, Kest, collapses at the river ford, pursued by ash-priests. He claims he swore an oath beside her mother twenty years ago and that the prophecy names Yara the Ember who will reignite the war. Emotional beat: distrust sharpening into reluctant alliance; grief for a mother she thought she knew.

chapters.title: Ash-Priests in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The ash-priests reach Emberhollow, and their leader, Vessic, offers the valley a bargain: surrender the Ember and the ward holds. Yara watches her neighbors consider handing her over. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being a sacrifice in a community she loves.

chapters.title: Oathbound, Broken
chapters.summary: Kest's POV. Kest recounts the last night of the swordspeakers: how Yara's mother shattered the original oath to hide her daughter in the one place magic couldn't find her, and what it cost him. Emotional beat: guilt and tenderness; the reveal that Yara's survival was purchased with a broken vow.

chapters.title: The Book Rewrites Itself
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The prophecy begins writing new lines in real time—Yara's own words appearing on the page before she speaks them. She realizes the book isn't predicting her; it's steering her. Emotional beat: terror of losing authorship of her own life, and defiance kindling beneath it.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Elder Maren admits the valley's founders were swordspeakers who built the ward as a prison for their own power—and that every generation, one child is quietly watched in case the ember survives. Maren has been her jailer and her guardian both. Emotional beat: betrayal transmuted into complicated forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Ward
chapters.summary: Yara and Kest's alternating POV. Vessic attacks the valley to force the prophecy's hand; Yara deliberately shatters the ward, letting magic flood Emberhollow to save her neighbors. Emotional beat: the irreversible choice—trading home and safety for agency, knowing there is no going back.

chapters.title: The Spire for the Ember
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the ash-priests' spire, the prophecy demands Yara speak the war-god's name into the blade and begin the war anew. Instead she speaks her own name, and the sword answers her rather than the book. Emotional beat: the climax—self-definition as an act of violence against fate itself.

chapters.title: A Valley Without Walls
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with a closing passage from the prophecy book itself. The war-god sleeps unbound; magic returns to the world unowned by any oath. Yara, no longer the last of anything, helps rebuild Emberhollow open to the sky. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—inheritance reclaimed as choice, and a home that must be remade rather than defended.
